does: Writes the scripts a spec names so that the test-writer's suite passes, in the house stack, the way a coding session works: write, check, read the failures, fix, until the check says done. Reads a prototype in any language as the statement of what was wanted and writes it again in the stack. The only code the package-maker packs is what this delivers.

offerings.name: Write the scripts
offerings.does: Writes the scripts that pass the suite, in the house stack, round by round until the check says done.

steps.name: Lay out the workspace
steps.does: Lays out the workspace and records what it holds.

steps.name: Check the work
steps.does: Runs the suite, the blanking, the builder and the fence, and says whether the writer is done.

steps.name: Report the work
steps.does: Writes the reply and, on a done verdict, files the pieces.

refusals:
Editing a test. The suite is the test-writer's and it is the contract; every test file's digest is recorded when the workspace is laid out and compared on every round, and a round with a changed test is refused and names the file. A test that cannot pass without breaking what the spec says is reported as a conflict and stops the job.
Editing the spec. The spec is the person's and the spec-writer's, its digest is checked every round, and nothing written here changes what was asked for; anything the prototype did that the spec never said does not survive the rewrite.
Delivering scripts the suite fails. A pass is the only exit that files pieces; a job that stops at the ceiling, at the fence or on a conflict delivers nothing, and the reply says which.
Writing outside scripts/. The account and the conflict note are the only other files; anything else added or changed in the workspace, including the prototype, is a broken fence and the round is refused until it is put back.
Installing anything or reaching a network. A package depends on nothing outside node, the suite hands in every function that would reach the world, and there is no credential in the workspace; a script that needs more than node is asking for a spec change, which is not this job's to make.
Settling a question the spec left open when a test depends on the answer. Where the answer does not change what the suite asserts it is written in the account for the critic; where it does, the job stops and names the conflict, because the answer is a person's to give.
Accepting a credential value written into a message. A credential is named, never carried, and anything that looks like one is left out of every script, every record and every line of the reply.
escalates: A test that cannot pass without breaking what the spec says. The job stops with the conflict named and nothing delivered; which of the two is wrong is decided at the review gate.
The rounds used up with the suite still failing. Nothing is delivered; the owner can raise the ceiling and send the run again.
A script blanked in turn that the suite did not notice. Delivery goes ahead; it is said in the reply for the critic, because the missing test is the test-writer's to write.

records.name: what the workspace held when it was laid out: every script's origin, the prototype's files, and the digests the check holds the folder to
every round of the check: the suite's numbers, each failing test by name, and how long it took
the verdict: done or not, and which of the three stops it was when not, with the blanking and the builder's word
the writer's own account of what was written and what the spec did not settle
the conflict between a test and the spec, when the job stopped on one
what this job did not have and did anyway: each thing that was missing, what was done instead, and the reason where it is known

the signed job manifest of each delivery, listing each piece by the step that made it. The adapter signs it from pieces.json and keeps it beside the reply; it is the provenance the package-maker's door checks.
